title: Darnassus
body: Darnassus is the capital of the night elves, raised in the high boughs of the World Tree Teldrassil off the northern coast of Kalimdor. After the Battle of Mount Hyjal cost the kaldorei their immortality, druids led by Fandral Staghelm grew the tree, and the city took root in its branches as a monument to their people's survival. Unlike the stone cities of men and dwarves, it lies open to the sky. Its halls stand far apart among groves and leafy paths, and a quiet lake at its heart is crossed by graceful bridges. Ancients and Sentinels keep watch, and a portal in the west carries travelers down to Rut'theran Village. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind rules from the Temple of the Moon, while Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm leads the druids from the Cenarion Enclave, and the two do not always agree. The tree's growth remains flawed, and a quarrel simmers between Darnassus and the druids of Moonglade.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Darnassus (founding after the Third War, open to the sky, buildings set apart, central lake and bridges, portal from Rut'theran)

title: Cenarion Enclave
body: In the northern reaches of Darnassus lies the Cenarion Enclave, home of the city's druids. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm holds court in the great tree at its heart, and his second, Mathrengyl Bearwalker, trains young druids on the level below and answers the callers the Arch Druid would rather not see. Hunters learn their craft here from Jocaste and Dorion, while in a quieter corner the rogue trainers Syurna and Erion Shadewhisper keep to the shadows. Lelanai tends the nightsabers the Sentinel army has long relied upon, offering them only to proven friends of Darnassus. Behind the Arch Druid's tree, Jenal the ditch digger guards heaps of Un'Goro soil, and Rellian Greenspyre walks the pathways deep in thought.

title: Craftsmen's Terrace
body: The Craftsmen's Terrace, in the northeast of Darnassus, gathers the city's artisans: alchemists, enchanters, tailors, leatherworkers, skinners and cooks, heirs to a millennium of knowledge. Young adventurers keep them busy with constant orders for supplies. Innkeeper Saelienne bids the weary rest beneath her roof and let Elune guide their dreams, and Lysheana charters new guilds. Envoys of the Argent Dawn keep a post here, gathering rumors that the Twilight's Hammer and the naga have joined forces in Blackfathom Deeps, once a night elf temple with a powerful moonwell. A small library holds histories of the War of the Ancients, the World Tree and the Emerald Dream, and the Old Gods.

title: Warrior's Terrace
body: The Warrior's Terrace spreads inside the city's gate, where an Ancient of War stands guard and Sentinels keep watch. Arias'ta and Darnath Bladesinger teach the warrior's art, and Elanaria tests the most promising before taking them as pupils. The smith Mathiel works elunite, a metal blessed by Elune herself, and Ilyenia Moonfire teaches the bow, the staff and other weapons. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver, a commander of the Sentinels, keeps her post here. Battlemasters gather volunteers for Warsong Gulch, Arathi Basin and Alterac Valley.

title: Tradesmen's Terrace
body: South of the Warrior's Terrace lies the Tradesmen's Terrace, the market of Darnassus. Its auctioneers take bids from across the Alliance, and its merchants sell blades, bows, staves, robes, mail and much else, while Talaelar offers the catch of the lake. The fishermen of Teldrassil moved here when attacks made Lake Al'Ameth unsafe, and Astaia teaches the angler's craft by the water. Among these homes lives Treshala Fallowbrook, whose husband went far away into the Barrens. In a locked chest the Sentinels keep the belongings of the priestess Velinde Starsong, who vanished from her post in Ashenvale, and a copy of The Betrayer Ascendant, telling how Illidan turned to demonic power after his release, waits for any reader.

title: The Temple Gardens
body: West of the Warrior's Terrace, across a causeway, lie the Temple Gardens, where Sentinels stand watch along every path. Firodren Mooncaller teaches herbalism among the flower beds, and Herald Moonstalker cries the latest news from both continents, from calls to arms in the Plaguelands to the frontiers of Kalimdor. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker of the Explorers' League keeps his post here. Beyond the gardens to the west, a portal carries travelers down to Rut'theran Village. To the south a further causeway leads to the Temple of the Moon, the heart of the night elves' faith.

title: Temple of the Moon
body: The Temple of the Moon is the seat of the Sisters of Elune and the true center of power in Darnassus. At its heart a statue rises from a moonwell, its holy waters said to purify and cleanse corruption. Tyrande Whisperwind keeps her quarters on the upper level. Priestesses such as Astarii Starseeker, Jandria and Alathea teach those who follow Elune, while the scholar Gracina Spiritmight studies the threats rising in the south. Visitors are greeted with Elune's blessing, and the temple's teachers offer their wisdom and knowledge to those who seek it.

title: Tyrande Whisperwind
body: Tyrande Whisperwind, High Priestess of Elune, rules Darnassus from the Temple of the Moon. Ten thousand years ago she stood against Queen Azshara in the War of the Ancients, and through the long ages while the druids slept she led the Sentinels in guarding the forests. In the Third War she woke Malfurion from his long slumber, freed Illidan from his prison against Malfurion's wishes, and fought beside humans and orcs at Mount Hyjal against Archimonde. She often clashes with Fandral Staghelm, the Arch Druid who leads the druids. She greets seasoned heroes warmly and asks them to share their tales with the young.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Tyrande_Whisperwind (War of the Ancients, Long Vigil, Third War, freeing Illidan, Hyjal, clashes with Fandral, sole leader with Malfurion gone)

'Lost in the Emerald Dream' made 'no one knows what became of him', as 933 has it (the Dream is told only in the Moonglade and Silithus Eranikus quests, 8734). parts.body: Malfurion Stormrage is not at her side. After Hyjal he vanished, and to this day his people do not know what became of him. So Tyrande rules Darnassus alone, while Fandral Staghelm leads the druids in Malfurion's place.
sources: quest 933 reward text (Shan'do Stormrage never returned; no one knows what became of him; Fandral took over the druids)

title: Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm
body: Fandral Staghelm is the Arch Druid of Darnassus. A thousand years ago he led the night elves against the Qiraji in Silithus, who named him Khar'sis, hand of the earth. Today he leads the druids of Darnassus, and after Hyjal he won the Circle of Ancients over and grew Teldrassil, hoping to win back his people's lost immortality. Proud and short of patience, he scorns idle visitors and says it was he, not Moonglade, who led his people out of darkness.
sources: creature_text 15183 (Geologist Larksbane: Khar'sis; no script says it in this core)
page_text 2794-2797 (father and son, Southwind fell, arrogance snuffed out)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Fandral_Staghelm (War of the Shifting Sands; archdruid after Malfurion; Teldrassil)
quest 940 reward text (work never completed, immortality never restored)
quest 6761 description (led us out of the darkness, not Moonglade)
notes: Converted: the dragons' refusal (Teldrassil gates it behind DONE 7383) and Malfurion's disappearance (DONE 929/933) moved out of the opening into part 1 on QUEST_DONE 935, where Fandral receives the water (935's own description tells the dragons' refusal); the yoke goes with it. Teldrassil left 935 and 940 to Darnassus: part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 940) tells the Oracle Tree's message (the calm, the forest's promise), part 3 (QUEST_DONE 940) Fandral's reading of the report. DONE 935 and 940 stay entry triggers too. The opening keeps the Silithus history, his leadership and the Circle's approval (told in Teldrassil's zone opening), and his temper (npc_text 2285, 6761 description). Nothing of his later fate. creature_text 15183 (Larksbane) and 15341 (Rajaxx) reread: patch 1.9 text, nothing from Cataclysm. Earlier: Verified. 'A thousand years ago' confirmed by General Rajaxx's own line in the 3.3.5 data. Faction 1: template 80. 935 and 940 are turn-ins only; Teldrassil's Crown of the Earth and Oracle's Messenger use 920, 921 and 937, and this entry does not retell them. Stormrage novel and Cataclysm material absent. Check: Valstann's death moved from the opening to part 1 on QUEST_ACCEPT 8303: no Darnassus NPC, quest, gossip or book tells it; in 3.3.5 it comes only from Silithus, where Larksbane's reading (creature_text 15183) has no script and is never said, so the real source is the tome The War of the Shifting Sands (item 20415), handed out as 8303's StartItem. The part follows the tome, so the trap and the execution by Rajaxx before his father's eyes (only in the unsaid Larksbane text) were dropped; Rajaxx's own taunt (creature_text 15341 group 3, Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj) is left to an instance file. Fix: the ACCEPT 8303 part (Valstann, from the War of the Shifting Sands book) was removed, since 8303 belongs to Silithus's Scepter chain; Valstann's death is left to Silithus. Opening: 'took up the leadership of the druids' after Hyjal (which hints at Malfurion's absence, Teldrassil's DONE 933 reveal) made 'leads the druids'. The 940 accept part reworded to start from Fandral (the reports the tree sends him). Far-off person triggers follow the converted files (thunder_bluff 163811 DONE 2280, ironforge 153702 ACCEPT 4362, wetlands 1131 DONE 943).

parts.body: The water of Teldrassil's moonwells reaches him at last, poured into one vessel in Dolanaar after the long telling of the tree's making: how Malfurion Stormrage vanished after Hyjal and never returned, and how the dragons Alexstrasza and Nozdormu refused their blessing, leaving its growth flawed. Fandral grumbles at the slow delivery and the choice of messenger. The weight of Teldrassil's problems falls on his shoulders, he says, a yoke he wishes he could soon be rid of.
sources: quest 935 description, completion and reward text
quests 929, 933, 7383 reward texts (the earlier steps of the chain)

parts.body: The Oracle Tree, which watches over Teldrassil's growth, sends its reports to him, but none has come for a long while: its last runner was slain by harpies, and the tree has feared sending another. Once the harpies are driven from their nests and a greater calm spreads through the forest, the tree entrusts its message for the Arch Druid to the one who freed it, promising that the forest will see its bearer safely along its paths to the forest of stone.
sources: quest 940 description (offered at the Oracle Glade after 937; the tree has feared sending another messenger)

parts.body: Fandral reads the report and understands why the tree has kept silent for so long. Some of Teldrassil's problems are lessened, he finds, while others grow into greater concerns, and he fears his work on the tree will never be completed, nor his people's immortality restored.

title: Mathrengyl Bearwalker
body: Mathrengyl Bearwalker is the Arch Druid's second and one of the druid trainers of the Cenarion Enclave, keeping to the level below Fandral Staghelm's chamber. He welcomes young druids as brothers and sisters and reminds them that they are the preservers of the balance, now and forever, as Cenarius taught. He also sees to the business his master would rather not handle himself. When the call for help came from Moonglade, the Arch Druid handed it to him, and he hands out the seeds for the Arch Druid's research and gathers what grows from them, asking only that Fandral not be disturbed with every batch.
sources: npc_text 4786 (preservers of the balance as Cenarius taught)
quest 3781 reward text, 3785 description, 3803 reward text (uncomfortable near morrowgrain)
DB: Mathrengyl 4217 subname Druid Trainer, gossip menu 1403
notes: Converted: his apology and the mistrust between Fandral and Remulos (6761 reward text) moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 6761, turned in to him; his unease near the morrowgrain (3803 reward text) to part 2 on QUEST_DONE 3803 (auto-complete). The opening keeps his role (npc_text 4786, 6761 and 3781, 3785 descriptions). npc_text 4786 reread: classic. Earlier: verified. Faction 1: template 80. 'Chief trainer' is general; he is one of three druid trainers. His morrowgrain quests are used as story context only (no triggers).

parts.body: Mathrengyl apologizes for his master's welcome to Moonglade's volunteers. The air is thick with mistrust between the Arch Druid and Keeper Remulos, he admits, each suspecting the other of trickery, and the strange corruptions of Teldrassil that go on unabated do little to ease it. Yet duty to the Cenarion Circle remains, even if its leaders disagree, though he warns the tensions may grow.

The morrowgrain troubles him more than he lets on. He takes the harvest ten at a time for the Arch Druid, but confesses that simply standing near the herb makes him uneasy, and he wonders how Fandral can bear to keep so much of it.
sources: quest 3803 completion and reward text (auto-complete, so QUEST_DONE)

title: Gracina Spiritmight
body: Gracina Spiritmight is a priestess of the Temple of the Moon and a scholar who has spent long years studying the creatures unique to Azeroth, a historian besides. She is an associate of Shandris Feathermoon's Protectorate, and when strange insects are reported in the deserts of Tanaris or the forests of Feralas, it is to her that the reports are sent, in the hope that she can say what the threat is and, more importantly, how it might be stopped.
sources: quest 4267 description, request and reward text (priestess, Protectorate, Shandris)
quest 4508 request and reward text (Alliance, Darnassus leaders, Fandral)
notes: Converted: her naming of the silithid (162, 4267 reward texts) moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 162 and 4267 (both turned in to her; Tanaris and Feralas leave them unused); her Un'Goro theory to part 2 on QUEST_ACCEPT 4493 (from her; Tanaris leaves March of the Silithid to the capitals); her railing at the Alliance and Fandral and the stronger presence to part 3 on QUEST_DONE 4508 and QUEST_ACCEPT 4510 (4510 follows 4508). The opening is her standing and why the reports come to her (162, 4267 descriptions). Earlier: 'Traced' softened to 'suspected' (4493 is a theory). 4508 is QuestSortID 440 (Tanaris) but ends with Gracina in Darnassus; Tanaris must not reuse its turn-in. Rest verified. Check: part 3 softened to the text ('not sure what good it will do'; 'a far stronger presence somewhere'). DONE 162, DONE 4267 and ACCEPT 4493 used by no other file; tanaris.json and feralas.json note them unused, ungoro.json uses ACCEPT 4496.

parts.body: Gracina knows the creatures at once. The night elves know this terror, she says: the insects are the silithid, and they will consume the land rapidly. They are no mere pests but the tools of one of the greatest threats that both Horde and Alliance will ever face.

Her theory is that the silithid exist to devour everything in their path that is not of their kind, and that what has been seen so far is only the first stage. She suspects their strength comes from deeper in Kalimdor, from Un'Goro Crater, and sends word of it to Alchemist Pestlezugg in Gadgetzan.

Gracina doubts Pestlezugg's report will do much good. She rails that the Alliance sees no enemy but the Horde and that even the city's leaders cannot agree on the danger: Fandral Staghelm, she says, denies the silithid are the ancient threat she claims, and his ignorance is surpassed only by his arrogance. She now fears her guess about Un'Goro was wrong, and that a far stronger presence lies somewhere else.

title: Rellian Greenspyre
body: Rellian Greenspyre is a druid of Darnassus, more often found walking the pathways of the Cenarion Enclave than resting in its halls. He is a friend of the herbalist Denalan, who camps on the shore of Lake Al'Ameth to study the sickly timberlings of Teldrassil, and he took an early interest in that work, with ideas of his own. His hope was to grow a timberling from a seed, and so help his friend in the search for a cure.
notes: Converted: Teldrassil left Rellian's findings to Darnassus. The seeds carrying the taint and the culling order moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 922 (turned in to him; 923 is offered at once), the tumors as a poison to part 2 on QUEST_DONE 923, the summons back to Denalan to part 3 on QUEST_ACCEPT 2498 (Flags 8, QuestType 2, not auto-complete). What Denalan found (Oakenscowl) stays with Teldrassil (ACCEPT 2499). The opening is his interest and his idea (922 description and the start of its reward text). Earlier: Reframed to avoid retelling Teldrassil's Tainted Timberlings (14128) and Denalan (14119): the taint passing to seeds, the Wellspring Lake culling and the 'only hope' line are left to them. Faction 1: template 80.

parts.body: A seed from the lake ended that hope. A corruption has grown in many of the timberlings, Rellian found, and seeds from such creatures carry their parents' taint, beyond his talents to repair. Denalan, so skilled with growing things, may be the timberlings' only hope. Until the source is found, those beyond help must be cut down, and the most tainted of all wander Wellspring Lake in northern Teldrassil.

The mossy tumors cut from the timberlings of Wellspring Lake are brought to him to be burned. They are the symptom of the timberlings' disease, he says, and they are filled with a poison that must be cleansed from the new land.

Then word reached him from the lake: Denalan had discovered what may be causing the tumors that plague the timberlings. Rellian wasted no time, and sent help to his friend at once with a plea for haste, for Denalan needed their aid.

title: Syurna
body: Syurna trains rogues in the Cenarion Enclave and has nothing to say to anyone outside her craft; her order, she says, is darkness and shadows, eternal and invisible. She has an admirer she never asked for. Jannok Breezesong, who trains rogues in Dolanaar, is hopelessly lovestruck with her. His home is full of her portraits, he goes days without eating or sleeping as he laments the love they might have had, and since she will not see him, he sends her flowers by any courier he can find.
sources: DB: Jannok Breezesong 3599 spawn 9790,943 = area 186 Dolanaar
notes: Converted: Teldrassil left 2241 and 2242 to Darnassus. Her remark on the flowers and the errand to Sethir moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 2241, QUEST_ACCEPT 2242; 2242 has no prerequisite, so both are listed); Sethir's journal and the Darkshore sickness to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 2242). The opening keeps her gossip (npc_text 4793, 4794) and Jannok's devotion (2241 description, the premise of a rogue quest offered in Dolanaar). Both quests are rogue only (AllowableClasses 8). Earlier: Jannok 3599 stands in Dolanaar (186), not Shadowglen: fixed. 'No words for anyone else' softened (npc_text 4793 refuses non-rogues). Sethir detail cut to a general allusion since teldrassil.json 14125 tells it from 2242. Faction 1. Check: part 1 split: ACCEPT 2242 has no prerequisite (PrevQuestID 0, exclusive group 2206 with the other rogue starter quests 2206, 2238), so a rogue can take it without 2241 and never see the flower remark; the remark is now part 1 (DONE 2241), the Sethir errand part 2 (ACCEPT 2242), the journal part 3 (DONE 2242).

parts.body: Had she kept every flower that dolt sent her, Syurna remarks, she could have opened a shop. His gifts mean nothing to her, but his latest courier may prove useful, and she has work in mind for those of her craft.

Her order wants to know what is happening to the forests of Teldrassil, and one being may know: Sethir the Ancient, a satyr hiding on a branch at the edge of the Oracle Glade. All who approached him, by force or diplomacy, met their doom, so she asks a young rogue to try stealth instead and learn what he carries in his packs.

From Sethir's packs comes a journal written in a tongue its bearer cannot read, but Syurna draws grim news from it. The sickness that has gripped the forests and rivers of Darkshore, she says, has begun to taint Teldrassil itself. There is nothing more her helper can do there, and she rewards the service with a blade.
sources: item 7737 Sethir's Journal (written in a language you cannot decipher)

title: Thyn'tel Bladeweaver
body: Thyn'tel Bladeweaver is one of the commanders of the Sentinels, keeping her post on the Warrior's Terrace. Into her keeping came the belongings of Velinde Starsong, the priestess who held back the demons of Felwood from Ashenvale until her efforts faltered little by little and one day she simply vanished. Velinde's things, among them a journal of her duties, lie locked in a chest, and Thyn'tel will not speak of the priestess's departure to a stranger without good reason. The Sentinels believe Velinde had her own reasons for leaving and could return at any time, for she did much to earn their trust.
notes: Converted: Velinde's death in Duskwood and the loss of the Scythe of Elune removed from the opening: they are Duskwood's reveal (duskwood.json 1028 part 2) and the Scythe chain (1022 on) belongs to Ashenvale, so no Darnassus trigger can carry them and no part is added. Thyn'tel's reading of the journal (1038 reward, mid-chain) dropped for the same reason. The opening keeps Velinde's vanishing (1037 description), the locked chest and journal and the Sentinels' belief (1038 description), and her friendship with Tyrande. Earlier: verified. Faction 1: template 80. The Scythe of Elune chain (1022 onward) starts and ends in Ashenvale and Duskwood's quests; only the TALK trigger is used, leaving the quests to Ashenvale. Duskwood's 1028 already covers Velinde's death at Roland's Doom. Check: Velinde's friendship with the high priestess removed: it is told only in the 1044 reward text, the moment her fate is revealed (Duskwood's 1028 part 2), and no Darnassus trigger reaches it.

title: Archmage Mordent Evenshade
body: Archmage Mordent Evenshade is an envoy of the Highborne, the night elf sorcerers who have hidden for ages in the ruins of Eldre'Thalas and are now drawn out by a change on the wind. He has come to the Temple of the Moon to seek an accord with Tyrande Whisperwind, and he waits for his audience under the cold eye of Sentinel Stillbough, who reminds him that the kaldorei have not forgotten the War of the Ancients or the minds behind it. Mordent concedes that the lure of power is great and that mistakes were made. Still, he will not leave until he is heard, warning that the kaldorei may soon need the knowledge his people keep.
sources: quest 14409 description and reward text (Daros Moonlance, ruins of Eldre'Thalas, change is coming)
notes: Converted for eras: requiredState 13 on the entry, as undercity.json did for Bragor (149706): Mordent and Daros arrived in patch 3.3.0 and Mordent stands in the temple in every era in this database (not phased by mod-individual-progression), so nothing in the entry is true before Wrath. Part 1 added on QUEST_DONE 14409 (already an entry trigger), from its reward text. creature_text 36479, 36481 and npc_text 14984 reread: patch 3.3 text; the Highborne's later acceptance (Cataclysm) is not claimed. Earlier: verified. Mordent 36479 is spawned in the temple by the moonwell with gossip 10807 (npc_text 14984: the Highborne are returning to light, not yet accepted); 14409 starts with Daros 36506 in Dalaran (template 80) and ends with Mordent. No readmission is claimed. Faction 1: Mordent and Daros 36506 (in Dalaran) both template 80, hostile to the Horde, though 14409 has AllowableRaces 0. Patch 3.3 content; the Highborne joining night elf society is Cataclysm and left out.

parts.body: A journal from his colleague Daros Moonlance, who studies the city of Dalaran, finds its way to him. Mordent welcomes it: Daros was always meticulous in tracking their progress, and his words may help explain how far the Highborne have come. Perhaps, Mordent says, they will be seen more often once it is understood that they mean no harm.

title: Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker
body: Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker represents the Explorers' League in Darnassus, keeping his post by the Temple Gardens. He is used to friends in the Alliance dismissing his work as a mere hobby, but he insists that recent discoveries in Khaz Modan prove a great and powerful force threatens all of Azeroth, from Lordaeron to Kalimdor. Of late, his own dig crew in Darkshore gives him cause to worry: they have not sent word in weeks.
notes: Converted: the fossil from Prospector Remtravel and Flagongut's theory removed: they are told at Darkshore's turn-in of 741 and in 942, mid-chain steps of the Remtravel chain, which belongs to Darkshore, so no Darnassus trigger may carry them. The opening keeps his premise from 730 and a general line on the League's conferences (942). Earlier: verified. Faction 1: template 55 (Ironforge), hostile to the Horde, although 730 has AllowableRaces 0. The Remtravel chain plays out in Darkshore and is left to it; no quest triggers used. Check: the line on the League's annual conferences (942 description, offered by him only after Darkshore's 741 turn-in, mid-chain of the Remtravel story Darkshore owns) removed.

title: Treshala Fallowbrook
body: Treshala Fallowbrook keeps a quiet home among the houses of the Tradesmen's Terrace, the market quarter of Darnassus, and she meets strangers at her door with polite surprise. Her husband, Heralath, went far from Teldrassil, across the sea to the Barrens and into Razorfen Kraul, the thorny warren where the quilboar make their home, a dangerous place even for the bravest of travelers.
sources: quest 1142 completion text (what brings you to my home)
DB: Heralath Fallowbrook 4510 starts 1142 in Razorfen Kraul; Treshala 4521 ends it, spawn in area 1662
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Razorfen_Kraul (quilboar warren of thorny vines in the Barrens)
notes: Converted: Heralath's death, the pendant and Treshala's grief moved from the opening to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 1142 (turned in to her; already an entry trigger). The opening keeps her home and that her husband went to Razorfen Kraul. 1142's start belongs to the Barrens and is not used. Earlier: verified. Faction 1: template 80; 1142 AllowableRaces 1101. Razorfen Kraul is QuestSortID 1717 and belongs to the Barrens, so only the turn-in is used. Heralath's work is not specified in the text. Check: 'on work of his own' removed: Heralath's work is named only in the 1142 reward text (part 1).

parts.body: Heralath never came home. Mortally wounded in the warren, he sent the dwarf Lonebrow to carry a warning to Falfindel, and with his last strength begged that Treshala's pendant of bonding, stolen by one of his attackers, be found and returned to her with word of his lonely death. When it reached her, she cried out that it was not fair. Sending the bearer away so that she might mourn alone, she swore that Heralath's work would not die with him.

title: The Arch Druid's Research
body: Innkeepers in the cities of the Alliance pass on a quiet request: the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus needs seasoned helpers for a vital research project, and none other than Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm is leading it. The Arch Druid explains it once and will not repeat himself, warning that those who think such errands beneath them will not win his favor. The soil of Un'Goro Crater is rumored to hold potent magic, and he means to separate fact from falsehood. Twenty loads are wanted from each helper, unloaded behind his tree for Jenal the ditch digger, who mutters that conspirators would keep a visionary like him shackled to obscurity.
sources: quest 3764 description, request and reward text
quest 3803 reward text (how the Arch Druid tolerates so much morrowgrain)
notes: Converted: the seeds and morrowgrain moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 3781, offered by Fandral after 3764), the first harvest to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 3785), Mathrengyl's unease to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 3803, auto-complete), as Thunder Bluff's Morrowgrain Research (163818) does. Era: the Exodar innkeeper (10520, Burning Crusade) is no longer named; the opening says innkeepers in the cities of the Alliance, true in every era. ACCEPT 10520 stays an entry trigger (draenei home ground). npc_text 2313 reread: classic. Earlier: Reworded to stand apart from thunder_bluff.json 163818 (Hamuul's Horde chain 3761, 3762, 936, 3784); this is the Alliance counterpart through Fandral, Jenal and Mathrengyl. Entry points confirmed: 3763, 3789, 3790, 10520 (Caregiver Breel, Exodar innkeeper) all reward into 3764, which Fandral gives. Faction 1: AllowableRaces 1101.

parts.body: The soil has a purpose. Fed with it in an evergreen pouch, costly Tharlendris seeds blossom into a scatter of potent herbs, and among them is morrowgrain, a mysterious herb about which little is known and which Fandral means to unravel. His second, Mathrengyl Bearwalker, sells the seeds in the enclave below.

Mathrengyl takes in the harvest for the Arch Druid's research and asks that Fandral not be disturbed each time a batch comes in. The need for morrowgrain, he says, is constant for now, and the mysterious properties of Un'Goro Crater grow clearer with each passing day.
sources: quest 3785 description, completion and reward text

parts.body: Batch after batch goes to him, ten at a time. Mathrengyl admits that simply standing near the herb makes him uneasy, and he wonders how the Arch Druid can bear so much of it. To what end it is gathered, Fandral does not say.
sources: quest 3803 completion and reward text (auto-complete, so QUEST_DONE)

title: The New Frontier
body: Heralds in Darnassus, Stormwind and Ironforge cry a summons: the Cenarion Circle seeks honorable proxies to explore a forbidden wasteland far west of Tanaris, and all who would answer should see Fandral Staghelm. Those who do are met with scorn. The Arch Druid asks why the welfare of all Teldrassil should wait on the hunt for some bauble, and calls the druids of Moonglade fools who waste his time. He hands the matter to his second, Mathrengyl Bearwalker, with a warning offered as friendly advice: it was he, not the Circle in Moonglade, who led their people out of darkness when all was lost, and Teldrassil gives them new life. To believe otherwise is to swallow propaganda.
notes: Converted: Mathrengyl's apology, the mistrust and the referral to Rabine moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 6761 (turned in to him; 6762 is offered at once). The opening keeps the summons (1047, 1015, 1019 descriptions), Fandral's scorn (their reward texts) and his advice (6761 description). Rabine and 6762 remain Moonglade's. Earlier: verified. Entry points 1047 (Darnassus), 1015 (Stormwind), 1019 (Ironforge), and 6761 which Fandral also offers directly. Faction 1: AllowableRaces 1101. Rabine's welcome and the Silithus expedition (6762 on, 1124) belong to Moonglade and Silithus; 6762 is not used as a trigger.

parts.body: Mathrengyl apologizes for the welcome. Mistrust runs thick between the Arch Druid and Keeper Remulos, he explains, each suspecting the other of trickery, but the Circle's work must go on. He sends the volunteers to Remulos' majordomo, Rabine Saturna, in Nighthaven, warning that the tensions between Darnassus and Moonglade may yet grow.

title: Lady Sathrah
body: Sister Aquinne, a novice of the temple, seeks help for a once great creature of the forest, and sends those who answer to Priestess A'moora in the Temple of the Moon. A'moora tells of Lady Sathrah, a spider beloved of Elune. Graceful and pure, she spun silver threads through the moonlight to catch the evening mist, and the silvery dew she gathered had strong healing powers and was kept in the temple. But of late Sathrah has fallen into madness on the northern borders of Teldrassil near Wellspring Lake, and even her future young are threatened. The priestess regrets what she must ask: Sathrah is beyond hope, her suffering must be ended, and her silvery spinnerets brought back to the temple.
sources: quest 2518 description, request and reward text
DB: Lady Sathrah 7319 spawns at 10980,1366 and 10994,1687 (northern Teldrassil)
notes: Converted: Sathrah's end and the offering at the fountain moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 2518), the sacrifice made to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 2520). The opening is the premise of 2519 and 2518. Earlier: verified. 2519 is the entry (2518 requires it). Faction 1: AllowableRaces 1101. Teldrassil has no Sathrah entry.

parts.body: It is done, and the forest mourns Lady Sathrah, though A'moora holds that it had to be. The spinnerets are to be laid at the temple's central fountain as an offering to Elune, whose holy waters purify and cleanse the corruption that drove the spider mad, so that the goddess may bless her and let her be reborn at peace.

The sacrifice is laid in the fountain. The loss of Lady Sathrah is distressing, A'moora says, but only in this way may she be reborn with a renewed spirit, and the priestess prays that Elune will willingly accept the offering.

title: Elanaria's Trial
body: When a young warrior of Teldrassil shows promise, their teachers send them on to Elanaria on the Warrior's Terrace of Darnassus, where their name already rings loudly. Before she will teach, she asks for proof of resolve. The satyr Vorlus Vilehoof has found one of the remote moonwells southeast of the Ban'ethil Barrow Den and splashes in its pure waters, defiling them with his filth, and only his horn will satisfy her. The path to the moonwell is well hidden, she warns, and only those who stay focused and alert will find it.
sources: quest 1684 description and reward text (starters Kyra Windblade 3598, Moon Priestess Amara 2151)
notes: Converted: Vorlus defeated and the Shade of Elura moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 1683, QUEST_ACCEPT 1686), Elura's peace and the elunite case to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 1686), Mathiel's work to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 1692, 1693, the latter auto-complete), the wyvern shells to part 4 (QUEST_ACCEPT 1710, warrior only, not auto-complete). The opening is the premise of 1684 and 1683. Earlier: 'The trainers' changed to 'their teachers' (1684 is also given by Moon Priestess Amara). 1684 starts in Teldrassil but ends with Elanaria, and 1683, 1686, 1692, 1693 all run through Darnassus. Faction 1.

parts.body: With Vorlus defeated and the moonwell cleansed, the training begins, and its next lesson is the forging of a warrior's weapon. Long ago a ship broke on the rocks near the Auberdine lighthouse in Darkshore, scattering crates of elunite ore across the seabed, and its captain, the Shade of Elura, cursed herself to guard the cargo for all time. She must be defeated and the lost ore gathered.
Elura's defeat grants her a long deserved peace, and Elanaria places the gathered elunite in a case for the smith Mathiel, whose forge stands just to the south on the same terrace.

Mathiel counts it an honor to work elunite, a metal blessed by the goddess Elune herself, and he sets to work at once shaping weapons from the ore for the pupil to choose among. Working it, he says, is both an honor and a pleasure.

In time Mathiel has other work for seasoned warriors. His colleague Furen Longbeard has made a discovery he is eager to test, and he seeks the sunscorched egg shells of the wyverns of Highperch in Thousand Needles, to render into a lacquer for the links of a new mail armor.
